column1: Shapes, assembly totals and tensor rotation
column2: Uniform box Ixx=m(b²+c²)/12. Rotate each tensor as RIRᵀ, add the parallel-axis terms m[(r·r)I−rrᵀ], and use rCoM=Σmᵢrᵢ/Σmᵢ.
Diagonalize the symmetric tensor I=Q diag(λ) Qᵀ and pass its principal moments and axes to the engine.

column1: Physical mass distribution of imported models
column2: Assign uniform density to the bounding box and use its center and solid-box inertia unless explicit properties are supplied.
Minimize Σ(fᵢ−mg/n)² subject to Σfᵢ=mg and zero roll/pitch moment about the CoM. A negative solution indicates required downward thrust.

column1: Frame mass allocation by primitive volume
column2: Assign mᵢ=mframe Vᵢ/ΣVⱼ using the plate plus the portions of the arms outside it.
Sum component masses and rotated tensors with the parallel-axis shift to the combined CoM.

column1: Gravity, frame transforms and rigid-body integration
column2: Transform body loads with R(q), add gravity, and update velocity before position. Free fall has Δz=−gt²/2 and vz=−gt.

column1: Friction, single-point rebound and resting contact timing
column2: Coulomb friction limits tangential impulse by μJn. Ideal normal rebound is vout=−e vin with apex e²h above contact.

column1: Fixed obstacle contact and initial overlap
column2: Unilateral contact uses the shape-to-obstacle gap. Centered box rest height is obstacle top plus box half-height.
Four corner normal impulses affect linear and angular speed. The diagnostic compares the first rebound apex to e²h.

column1: Ideal BLDC steady state and RK4 spin-up
column2: Vm=ω/Kv+RI, Qm=Kt(I−I₀), and Jω̇=Qm−kQω². Solve the steady quadratic or integrate with RK4.
Solve Vd²−(ω/Kv)d−RIpack=0 per bench row, then interpolate the monotone fitted duty map.
Fit fx²+(1−f)x to (ω(x)/ω(1))² by least squares with f constrained to [0,1].
Fit T=kTω² with kT=Σ(Tω²)/Σω⁴.
Infer Q=Kt(Ipack/d−I₀), then fit Q=kQω² by least squares.
Fit T=kTω² and Q=kQω² to the applicable APC static table rows.

column1: Rotor loads, reaction, gyroscopic and density scaling
column2: Sum r×T, shaft reaction and rotor angular-momentum terms. Scale the static thrust and torque coefficients by ρ/ρref.

column1: Pack sag, charge use and configured cutoff
column2: Vpack=Voc−RintΣI and charge used is ∫ΣI dt. The configured cutoff interrupts drive.
Along each axis, estimate the area of the union of the projected shapes on two raster resolutions.
Fᵢ=−ρCd,ᵢAᵢ|vrel,ᵢ|vrel,ᵢ/2 in body axes.
vrel=vbody−vwind in a common frame. A wind bearing gives the direction it comes from.
The gust rises as A[1−cos(πs/L)]/2 with s accumulated using start-of-step mean-air-relative speed, then holds at A.
U(z)=Uref log(z/z₀)/log(zref/z₀) on the profile interval with endpoint handling.
Advance the Dryden filter states with their discrete linear transition and Gaussian innovations. Check variance and spectral density.
Filter length scales Lᵢ and intensities σᵢ depend on clearance and the entered reference wind. Hold at the supported height endpoints.
In hover, TIGE/TOGE=1/[1−(R/4Z)²] in the formula’s domain. Induced velocity follows the momentum balance.
Evaluate the single-rotor thrust ratio at each hub’s clearance and scale the rotor thrust.

column1: Grid ingest, triangle height and engine registration
column2: Compute surface height by barycentric interpolation in the selected heightfield triangle and transform grid coordinates to the engine frame.
Clearance follows shape support relative to the ground. The Coulomb slide/rest threshold is tan(slope)=μ.
Fly the takeoff, hold and landing state sequence against the terrain heightfield. Evaluate hold error, touchdown speed and the landed state.
Allocate u=B⁺w from the rotor-effectiveness matrix B and normalize the selected allocation axes.
Adjust motor commands by gains along selected allocation directions, then clip to the command range.
For desired normalized thrust t, invert t=fu²+(1−f)u on [0,1].
τ=Kp(ωsp−ω)+I−Kdω̇+Kffωsp. Saturation gates integrator growth.
Align the thrust axes first, weight the residual yaw, then map the canonical quaternion error’s imaginary part to a rate demand.

column1: Position P, velocity PID, thrust vector and limits
column2: vsp=vff+Kp,pos(psp−p). Velocity PID plus acceleration feed-forward yields a thrust vector limited by tilt and thrust constraints.
Compare the vertical response and state hash to the legacy controller fixture.

column1: Manual stick shaping and trajectory smoothing
column2: Apply deadband and expo to the stick, map to tilt or velocity, and integrate a jerk-limited trajectory under velocity and acceleration constraints.

column1: Integrated hover, payload and trim scenarios
column2: Compare steady thrust and moment balance (ΣT=mg and Σr×T=0) with hover, loaded and offset-CoM scenarios.

column1: Takeoff state machine and signed climb ramp
column2: Run the takeoff state machine and ramp the signed climb limit from its initial value to the commanded climb speed.

column1: Auto takeoff, hold and land target equations
column2: Generate climb and hold setpoints, then interpolate descent speed between the configured height gates.
Run scripted target changes through the flight loop and check hold errors, touchdown and detector transitions.

column1: Altitude cone, straight-track trajectory and state order
column2: Combine the return altitude cone with altitude bounds, then follow a straight horizontal track under velocity, acceleration and jerk caps.
Follow climb → return → land → landed. Measure horizontal distance and vertical error relative to home.

column1: Ground contact, maybe-landed, landed and freefall predicates
column2: Combine thrust and motion predicates with state-dependent hysteresis. Evaluate freefall by its acceleration predicate.
Predict scalar variance with process noise, then update using K=PH/(H²P+R) when the innovation gate accepts the measurement.

column1: Static notch, two-pole low-pass and derivative alpha filter
column2: Apply notch and low-pass biquads, and first-difference the filtered rate before first-order smoothing.

column1: Noise-free filtered gyro feedback into the rate loop
column2: Compare the production filter path with separate direct-form I biquads and an alpha-smoothed rate derivative.

column1: Noisy gyro closed-loop hover and roll-rate response
column2: Compute RMS rate and tilt in hover and measure 10–90% rise time and overshoot in a rate step.

column1: IMU additive noise, vibration, bias walk and clipping
column2: Add vibration and Gaussian noise to truth, walk bias with variance proportional to elapsed time, then clip and delay the sample.
Rotate aCoM−g+α×r+ω×(ω×r) into the sensor axes.
Use the ISA pressure power law and its inverse; add pressure bias and noise before holding the sample.
Sample local CoM position and velocity on the configured cadence, deliver after the configured delay, and hold between deliveries.

column1: GPS stochastic error and barometer noise/bias calibration
column2: Perturb sensor truth with calibrated-input Gaussian noise and bias terms. The input calibration lacks independent observations.
Use T=T₀−Lh, p=p₀(T/T₀)^(g/RL) and ρ=p/(RT). For a temperature override, use the overridden temperature in density.
R=ρ·2L/A for the cable pair. Sum branch currents, subtract IR drops, and compute resistive losses as I²R.
Compare component limits, connector and port assignments, and geometric separation against the project rules.

column1: BLZR binary frames, corruption handling, persistence and export
column2: Check CRC-32 and complete-frame boundaries, recover the verified prefix, and export samples with the stored clock.
Keep chronological bucket minima and maxima with missing-value markers as specified by the point budget.

column1: Replay sample clock and window selection
column2: Use the last sample at or before the query time and clamp requested windows to the stored sample range.
Hold the stored pose between sample times. Re-simulate the recorded inputs and compare the saved outputs and hash.
XOR each ordered byte into the hash, then multiply by the FNV prime modulo 2⁶⁴.
